correctness.rationale: The rank-two normal form reduces exactly to P²=PQ=RP=RQ=0, over any field. Nonzero P has a unique image/kernel line and its projective incidence bundle is irreducible, dimension ab+a+b+2, and projects closedly; all P=0 points outside that component lie in precisely one of the two rank-two linear escape loci. Component containment and dimensions are proved by rank. Counting the q+1 line fibers and their common S-axis, then the two disjoint full-rank escape sets, proves the exact formula. Replay of actual standalone checker matched archived output for eight finite-field cases, including F4; this is corroborative rather than an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The square-zero set is a canonical algebraic subvariety of the finite Munn/sandwich semigroup. The theorem classifies every geometric irreducible component for arbitrary rectangular excess dimensions, computes all component dimensions and natural pairwise intersections, proves a sharp dominant-component transition at excess-size difference two, and gives a symmetric exact finite-field count for all prime powers. These motivated structural and arithmetic facts are not arbitrary table recomputations and identify a new rank-two boundary beyond the well studied rank-one and idempotent cases.
